about.title: Wildomar Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Riverside County recorded 3 traffic deaths in Wildomar in the most recent final crash year, alongside 91 injury collisions and 127 people hurt. Behind each number is a family left to sort through grief, funeral arrangements, and unanswered questions about how the crash happened. Corridors like Bundy Canyon Road, Clinton Keith Road, Palomar Street, and the I-15 southbound stretch see a steady share of the city's reported crashes, with Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. a common time for collisions to occur. California law allows certain surviving family members to pursue a wrongful death claim separate from any criminal proceeding against the at-fault driver. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect Wildomar families with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened, explain the options available, and help pursue accountability without adding to the family's burden.

about.ctaText: Speak with an independent attorney about your family's options.

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases, generally to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in some circumstances. An attorney can help determine who qualifies to bring the claim.

items.title: The Clock Starts Running Quickly
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity, such as a public road authority, may share fault. Waiting too long can permanently close the door on a claim.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial costs, lost financial support the deceased would have provided, and compensation for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. A civil wrongful death action proceeds separately from any related criminal case against the driver.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim after a crash in Wildomar?
items.answer: In California, the general deadline is two years from the date of death. If a government entity, such as one responsible for road maintenance on a corridor like Palomar Street, may be involved, a much shorter claim-filing window applies. It's important to act quickly so evidence isn't lost and deadlines aren't missed.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children typically have first priority to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may be eligible under certain circumstances. An independent attorney can review your family's situation and explain who has standing to pursue the claim.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, they are separate. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action a family pursues to recover financial losses and other damages. Both can move forward independently of one another.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to help our family?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects Wildomar families with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover compensation for you. We don't practice law ourselves; we simply make the connection.
